A Zener diode is normally operated in reverse breakdown for voltage regulation. Its selection centers on Zener voltage and power dissipation rather than rectifier reverse recovery.
A transient voltage suppressor diode clamps short overvoltage pulses. Important ratings include standoff voltage, breakdown voltage, clamping voltage, and peak pulse power.
A light-emitting diode emits light under forward bias. Selection includes color, luminous intensity, forward voltage, and allowable forward current.
A general rectifier diode converts alternating current to direct current. Reverse voltage, average current, surge current, forward drop, and recovery time can constrain replacement.
Package compatibility is independent from electrical adequacy. SOT23, SOD323, SOD-123W, SMA, and DO-41 footprints are not interchangeable without checking the PCB layout.
